thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High OOM rate observed on runtime-cluster-4 (gpu-nodepool) - 11 failures in 5m. Pager escalated to Sam (Oncall).

Sam (Oncall): I'm on it. Paging Jordan and Maya for GPU memory/kvcache triage. Anyone seeing traffic spikes?

Jordan (SRE): I'm looking at autoscaler and node metrics. No huge request spike. Network fine. Starting `nvidia-smi` snapshots across the pool.

Maya (ML Infra): Hypothesis: KV cache page swap/pinning causing fragmentation under certain batch shapes. Seen similar with long-chat workloads. Pulling recent runtime logs.

Ava (Runtime): Replaying a sample failing request now. If it's kvcache, we should see a rapid increase in vmem allocations then host OOMs.

Sam (Oncall): Customer impact: a handful of requests returned 500s intermittently for two customers (acct-redwood-x, acct-saas-pro). CS notified? @Lee

Lee (Customer Success): Notified both customers. They're seeing elevated latency then errors. Sharing a short summary to them, will update once we have mitigation.

Jordan (SRE): Paste of latest `dmesg` lines from a failed host:```
[ 1234.567890] Out of memory: Kill process 31415 (runtime) score 999 or sacrifice child
[ 1234.567895] Killed process 31415 (runtime) total-vm: 12345678kB, anon-rss: 9876543kB
[ 1234.568000] GPU 0: memory allocation failed: out of device memory
```

Maya (ML Infra): Good, GPU memory OOM + host OOM. That pattern matches kvcache growth then host swap exhaustion. Grabbed `kvecache` summary from the runtime:```
kvcache: entries=1.2M size=18.3GB active_ratio=0.78 pages=460 free_pages=12
kvcache_swap: hits=1245 misses=987 swapouts=120 swapins=48
```

Ava (Runtime): Also saw repeated large allocation traces in logs:```
2026-05-02T14:02:11Z runtime: alloc_gmm(346M) at step 24 seq_len=2048 batch=8 model=redopt-7b
2026-05-02T14:02:12Z runtime: kvcache_pin_page(id=0x7f3...) size=256M success=false
2026-05-02T14:02:12Z runtime: fallback_to_host_swap true
```

Sam (Oncall): Immediate mitigations? Can we reduce batch sizes or force kvcache eviction policy? We need to stop ongoing 500s.

Maya (ML Infra): Two quick actions: 1) apply a temporary server-side batch cap to 4 for runtime-cluster-4 routes; 2) set kvcache aggressive-evict=true for that cluster. I can push both in ~2-3 mins. Any objections?

Jordan (SRE): +1. Also recommend draining most memory-hungry pods from the impacted hosts after actions. I'll coordinate node drain once mitigations land.

Ava (Runtime): Pushing runtime config change now:```
PATCH /runtime/configs/cluster-4
{ "batch_limit": 4 }
```

Dev Deploy Bot: Config patch applied to cluster-4 (batch_limit=4) by Ava.

Maya (ML Infra): Enabling kvcache aggressive eviction flag:```
POST /infra/kvcache/cluster-4/eviction
{ "policy": "aggressive" }
```

Dev Deploy Bot: KV cache eviction policy updated for cluster-4 by Maya.

Sam (Oncall): Observability check: Jordan, can you watch OOMs and error rate, I'll monitor customer-facing errors in the dashboard.

Jordan (SRE): Watching. Initial telemetry: error-rate drops from 4.6% -> 2.1% within 60s of patch. OOM spikes down but still a couple of fails.

Maya (ML Infra): Also sementara workaround: rolling restart of a small subset (2/10) runtime pods on the worst hosts to free pinned pages. Scheduling now.

Ava (Runtime): Restarted pods: runtime-4-a, runtime-4-b. Logs show `kvcache_unpin` activity and host memory freed.

Sam (Oncall): Customer update sent: short note 'we're mitigating a memory issue, errors reduced, investigating root cause, will follow-up within 4 hours'.

Lee (Customer Success): Customers acknowledged — one asked if this could be due to quantized model change. They don't report config changes on their side.

Maya (ML Infra): Collecting detailed timeline for RCA: grabbing per-request traces, allocation histograms, and kvcache page-level metrics for the past 2 hours. Will paste artifacts here.

Jordan (SRE): Node-level snapshot:```
Host: gpu-node-14
CPU: 42% mem: 86% (swap used: 3.1G)
GPU0: total 48G used 44.2G free 3.8G
Processes: runtime(pid=31415) vmem=12G gpu_mem=40G
```

Ava (Runtime): Noted an odd correlation: failures concentrated on short bursts of long-sequence requests (seq_len >= 1500) interleaved with many small seq requests. Our batch packing seems to sometimes combine them, causing transient large allocations.

Maya (ML Infra): Hypothesis list (for RCA thread):
- H1: KV cache page pinning + insufficient eviction for mixed batch shapes -> fragmentation and host OOM.
- H2: Batch packing combined long seqs into same batch leading to peak GPU allocation > kernel-planned memory.
- H3: A recent runtime tweak to prefetch pages increased active_ratio causing less free pages for sudden peaks.
- H4: Underlying driver/kernel regression less likely but possible.

Sam (Oncall): Good hypotheses. For in-incident RCA we need owners: Maya -> H1/H3, Ava -> H2, Jordan -> H4/drivers & node-side.

Maya (ML Infra): I'll produce per-page churn graph and kvcache heatmap. Uploading S3 link: https://s3.redwood-internal/rca/1928501234/kvchurn.png

Ava (Runtime): Also uploaded a snippet of batch packing trace and the failing request example: https://s3.redwood-internal/rca/1928501234/batchpack.log

Jordan (SRE): Driver logs attached: https://s3.redwood-internal/rca/1928501234/driver-dmesg.log

Sam (Oncall): Current status: mitigations applied (batch cap + kvcache eviction + targeted restarts). Error rate down to 0.5% and OOM events normalized in last 10m. Moving to post-incident RCA phase.

Lee (Customer Success): I'll follow-up to say issue is mitigated and we'll share RCA when ready. Customers asked for ETA — I'll say 24-48h for full RCA.

Maya (ML Infra): Next steps for RCA doc: gather per-request mem histograms, candidate timeline, confirm if eviction policy change deworsened any perf; simulate long+short packing in test env to reproduce.

Ava (Runtime): I'll add an automated guard: refuse to pack sequences above 1024 with batch > 2 as a safety net while we fix packing heuristics. Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/834

Jordan (SRE): I'll coordinate a kernel/driver check on the hosts and schedule an additional burn test. If we see reproducer, escalate to infra infra-team.

Sam (Oncall): Thanks all. I'll close the pager and we will continue RCA in this thread — keep artifacts linked. Filing incident ticket: INC-2026-9047 and linking this thread.

Dev Deploy Bot: Incident INC-2026-9047 created by Sam (Oncall) -> https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-9047

Maya (ML Infra): Quick note for RCA: archive of relevant traces placed at https://s3.redwood-internal/rca/1928501234/archive.tar.gz

Ava (Runtime): I noticed one regression in the last runtime PR that adjusted prefetch thresholds (PR 780). Marking that for review in postmortem.

Jordan (SRE): Leaving a final status: hosts stabilized, no residual OOMs in 25m. Will do follow-up night scan for regressions.

Sam (Oncall): Closing active mitigations. If anyone sees a recurrence, re-pager. Thanks team :thumbsup:
